AI makes social activity easier, not obviously better
This chart comes from a 2025 experimental study on generative AI in social media. Across Control, Chat, Conversation, Feedback, and Suggestions, mean responses stay close to neutral on four questions: comfort with AI on social platforms, joining online discussions, making discussions less toxic, and reducing polarization.
The pattern is pretty consistent:
Feedback
tends to look a bit better, while
Chat
is usually the weakest condition. Sample sizes sit around
122–129
per group.
My read:
AI can help with volume and participation, but it does not automatically create better discussion quality. That is the same tension founder-led content runs into when the post sounds polished but not quite human.

arXiv

tweet.text:
Despite my bullish shitposting and current net long positioning, I’m actually decently bearish HTF.

I think float is likely to increase structurally as boomers become net sellers of equities, while weaker employment and lower participation among Zoomers make it harder for that supply to be absorbed.

More broadly, I think the growing degree of financial markets manipulation and macro intervention ultimately ends poorly (as it has so many times... just takes longer than people expect to play out). Most people probably recognize that faith in the system is deteriorating, but as long as liquidity keeps flowing into AI and asset prices keep going up, there’s little incentive to fight it.

Have been steadily buying physical gold every 2–3 weeks over the last few months as a hedge against some of these longer-term risks. I like owning something that doesn’t depend on the financial system functioning perfectly. And if I’m wrong, I can always just pass it down to my kids one day.

But for now

Vitalik Updates Ethereum Roadmap Prioritizing  Privacy, Quantum Safety, Native Rollups, and More
> Vitalik updated Ethereum's 2023 roadmap to reflect major new priorities: quantum safety, native rollups, strong privacy, and AI-accelerated formal verification, while noting several original items were reshuffled, deprioritized, or replaced with superior constructions.
Source:
https://x.com/VitalikButerin/status/2086824673556467938

tweet.text:
I updated my 2023 roadmap diagram to overlay where the items that were there sit in the current Strawmap ( https://strawmap.org/ ).

In general, a lot of overlap, but:

* Some things got reshuffled in order (eg. quantum safety up-prioritized)
* Some things deprioritized (eg. VDFs; many EVM improvements)
* Some things replaced with superior constructions (eg. Verkle -> unified BT -> PBT; state expiry -> new state types)

What's most striking, however, is that some completely new things are in the strawmap that are NOT in this diagram, because they were not in the 2023 roadmap at all. These reflect changing priorities.

Notably:

* First-class attention to strong privacy. This covers: keyed nonces and recent roots, aspects of FOCIL, lean privacy pool & wormholes
* Aggressive scaling in the context of post-quantum. This covers: leanSPHINCS signatures and aggregation, zkzk frames (see https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8288-frame-type-for-pq-sig-and-stark-aggregation/28723 )
* Lean-ifica

Vitalik Updates Ethereum Roadmap Prioritizing  Privacy, Quantum Safety, Native Rollups, and More
> Vitalik updated Ethereum's 2023 roadmap to reflect major new priorities: quantum safety, native rollups, strong privacy, and AI-accelerated formal verification, while noting several original items were reshuffled, deprioritized, or replaced with superior constructions.
Source:
https://x.com/VitalikButerin/status/2086824673556467938

tweet.text:
I updated my 2023 roadmap diagram to overlay where the items that were there sit in the current Strawmap ( https://strawmap.org/ ).

In general, a lot of overlap, but:

* Some things got reshuffled in order (eg. quantum safety up-prioritized)
* Some things deprioritized (eg. VDFs; many EVM improvements)
* Some things replaced with superior constructions (eg. Verkle -> unified BT -> PBT; state expiry -> new state types)

What's most striking, however, is that some completely new things are in the strawmap that are NOT in this diagram, because they were not in the 2023 roadmap at all. These reflect changing priorities.

Notably:

* First-class attention to strong privacy. This covers: keyed nonces and recent roots, aspects of FOCIL, lean privacy pool & wormholes
* Aggressive scaling in the context of post-quantum. This covers: leanSPHINCS signatures and aggregation, zkzk frames (see https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8288-frame-type-for-pq-sig-and-stark-aggregation/28723 )
* Lean-ifica

tweet.text:
Despite my bullish shitposting and current net long positioning, I’m actually decently bearish HTF.

I think float is likely to increase structurally as boomers become net sellers of equities, while weaker employment and lower participation among Zoomers make it harder for that supply to be absorbed.

More broadly, I think the growing degree of financial markets manipulation and macro intervention ultimately ends poorly (as it has so many times... just takes longer than people expect to play out). Most people probably recognize that faith in the system is deteriorating, but as long as liquidity keeps flowing into AI and asset prices keep going up, there’s little incentive to fight it.

Have been steadily buying physical gold every 2–3 weeks over the last few months as a hedge against some of these longer-term risks. I like owning something that doesn’t depend on the financial system functioning perfectly. And if I’m wrong, I can always just pass it down to my kids one day.

But for now
